undermines_explanation: I can't answer this question with a clear yes or no, so please do not take my selection as gospel. / It depends a lot on how the community engages with generated code. AI agents can either be used similar to previous code generation tools like protoc, SWIG, or linters, or they can nearly fully replace human work. And they can be used to replace understanding and deep research with. / My use of AI in coding has so far filled gaps: projects have bugs or missing features, the maintainers absolutely do not have time to train me to a point where I can solve those problems myself and they don't have time to triage bug reports, and I don't have enough motivation to keep my attention on someone else's project for long enough that I can teach myself their codebase deeply enough that I would be able to fix their bugs. In these cases there is little sense of community; instead, there is an elite class of the original developers, and they usually feel remote and austere. The only community in these projects is the community of *users*.  In I have asked AI to trace code for me to identify the sections relevant to the bugs/features, to give me starter code in languages/frameworks I am unfamiliar with, and occasionally to write fixes for me. So in this case I think using AI could enhance the community by expanding the community, by allowing the community of users to move into the community of developers. / But that's only possible if the community (developer and user together) is open to it. I think there is a lot of (understandable and justified) skepticism of the new era of tech feudalism, and in the avatars of Claude, Codex, Gemini and Kimi people are pretty worried about submission, about turning over their full agency to the new fascist era. In this sense, using AI absolutely undermines my sense of belonging to a community because it risks getting me run out with pitchforks and fire. / I also think that, in the extreme, projects that become fully directed by a single person plus their AI just become another kind of elitist bubble. Community is only possible if people are communicating and listening to each other; a project made by a single maverick person and supported by their LLM agents is not a project with a lot of sturdy roots.
